HUNT: partial. I executed nothing. After my first few read-only calls (git diff, reading src/tickets/spec.ts and src/frontmatter.ts, grepping callers), every Bash call failed with "server-side auto mode classifier gave no verdict (error)". That happened 9 times in a row, and one more would have ended my turn before I could report, so I stopped. What I didn't get to:
- `bun run check` and `bun test` in /Users/woueziou/works/personal_projects/worktrees/0042.
- The probe script (parse, serialize, parse again with quoting edge cases; two store-level moves; a v1 ticket with legacy and unknown keys; `createTicket`).
- A grep of the docs for leftover mentions of `ticket migrate --force`.

Every finding below comes from reading the code and is marked plausible. None has been reproduced. The probe was written and ready to run, and the two failures it targets are traced below through `src/frontmatter.ts` line by line.

What I checked by reading, with no problem found:
- **Legacy vs unknown keys:** `extraFrontmatter` filters out both `KEY_ORDER` and `LEGACY_KEYS` (issue/synced/syncedAt). A v1 ticket with `issue:` and `epic:` keeps `epic` and drops `issue`, and the two can't get mixed up.
- **Key order:** unknown keys keep the order they were in, because `Object.entries` preserves insertion order for string keys. They are always written after the known keys, so an `epic:` above `id:` moves down once on the first rewrite and then stays put.
- **Moving twice:** `ticket move` (`src/cli.ts:641`) spreads the parsed ticket, so `extraFrontmatter` comes along. The second move re-parses the first move's output and gets the same map.
- **`migrateTicket`:** it also spreads, so extras survive.
- **`createTicket`:** it sets `extraFrontmatter: {}`, and `serializeTicket` has an `?? {}` fallback. I found no other place that builds a `Ticket` from scratch in src/, and the dashboard doesn't dump whole ticket objects anywhere.
- **Quoting:** extra keys go through the same `quote`/`unquote` as known keys. Values with a colon, a leading `#` or single quotes round-trip correctly.

CHECK_OUTPUT: not obtained (classifier failure, see above). Neither `bun run check` nor `bun test` was run.

FINDINGS:
- (non-blocking) (plausible) src/frontmatter.ts:63 (`quote`), now reachable for any hand-added key through src/tickets/spec.ts:265.
  - **Defect:** `quote()` doesn't treat `\n`/`\r` as unsafe. A value that was JSON-escaped on read comes back from `unquote` with a real newline in it and is then written unquoted.
  - **Failure scenario:** a ticket carries `desc: "line1\nline2"` (a JSON-style escape inside a double-quoted YAML string). The next `ticket move` writes `desc: line1` followed by a bare line `line2`. On the next read `parseFrontmatter` throws "unparseable frontmatter line: line2". The ticket drops out of `listTicketsDetailed` into `errors`, and a later `ticket move` says "No ticket with id". If the second line happens to contain a colon, it silently becomes a new top-level key instead.
  - **Scope:** the same hole already exists for `title` today. This PR widens it to every free-form key, where escaped multi-line strings are more likely.
  - **Why not confirmed:** Bash was unavailable. The trace is `unquote` -> `JSON.parse` gives a real newline; `quote` checks `/: |:$| #|^\s|\s$/` and the leading-character class, and neither matches an embedded newline.
- (non-blocking) (plausible) src/tickets/spec.ts:158-166 and :265, together with the removed gates at src/cli.ts:587-597 and src/project-upgrade.ts:241-246.
  - **Defect:** the new doc comment promises "values as written", but only flat scalars keep their meaning. Other YAML shapes are rewritten into something different:
    - `tags: [a, b]` becomes `tags: "[a, b]"`, a string instead of a list, because the leading `[` triggers quoting.
    - `x: foo #note` becomes `x: "foo #note"`, so the comment is now part of the value.
    - A nested map (`meta:` followed by `  owner: bob`) becomes `meta: ` plus a new top-level `owner: bob`.
  - **Failure scenario:** before this PR, `litecode upgrade` skipped such a v1 ticket and `ticket migrate` refused without `--force`. Now both rewrite it without asking, and `ticket migrate` only prints a dim "keeps unknown frontmatter key(s)" line. That line suggests nothing changed while the file's meaning did change. `ticket move` used to drop these keys, so for move this is still an improvement. For migrate and upgrade it replaces a gate you could see with a silent change of type or structure.
  - **Scope:** narrow, since the parser's own header says exotic YAML is out of scope and the motivating keys (`epic`, `generated_by`, `task`) are scalars.
  - **Why not confirmed:** Bash was unavailable. The trace is `parseFrontmatter` (flat `key: value` per line, no comment stripping, indentation trimmed away), then `quote`'s leading-character class `[-?:,[\]{}#&*!|>'"%@`]`.

REENTRY:
- Finding 1 (newline in a value): same-PR fixup. Make `quote()` treat any `\n` or `\r` as unsafe, so the value is re-emitted as a JSON string. Add a round-trip test with an escaped newline in an extra key.
- Finding 2 (non-scalar values): new ticket via triage. Two options: have `extraFrontmatter` flag values or lines it can't carry faithfully (flow sequences or maps, indented continuation lines) and restore a warning or `--force` gate for those cases only; or narrow the doc comment to "flat scalar values". It's fine to defer if the owner accepts that hand-added keys must be scalars.
- Still open from the partial hunt: someone needs to run `bun run check`, `bun test` and the probes above in the worktree, and grep the docs, agents and skills for stale `migrate --apply --force` instructions, before relying on this report.
